paper_metadata.title: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping after Sports-Related Concussion

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population (high school and collegiate football athletes), recruitment methods across 10 institutions, and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria. Baseline characteristics are well-documented in Table 2.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Collegiate and high school football athletes were recruited at preseason team meetings at 10 local institutions.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the age group (high school/collegiate) and the specific athletic context (football) across multiple sites.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A subset of 56 subjects, split evenly across injured and matched control athletes, were enrolled into an advanced MR imaging component of the study during the season.
items.reasoning: The recruitment process from preseason meetings and the use of matched controls are described.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: enrolled... during the season.
items.reasoning: While it mentions 'during the season', specific calendar years for the recruitment period are not explicitly stated in the main text.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 10 local institutions... Medical College of Wisconsin, Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
items.reasoning: The geographic context and the type of institutions (local schools/colleges) are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Control subjects were excluded if they had a diagnosed prior concussion within 6 months of their initial imaging session. ... injured subjects were not excluded solely on the basis of prior concussions.
items.reasoning: The text details specific exclusion criteria for controls and the inclusion logic for injured subjects regarding prior history.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not provide the total number of eligible athletes at the 10 institutions versus those who consented, making it impossible to calculate a participation rate.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Tables 2 and 3 provide general characteristics of the complete study population.
items.reasoning: Table 2 includes age, weight, height, years in sport, GPA, and prior concussion history.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is notable attrition at the 6-month follow-up (e.g., SCAT severity n=19 vs n=28 at baseline). The authors acknowledge this as a limitation and assume data is missing at random, but do not provide a detailed analysis of those lost to follow-up.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: subject compliance for the MR imaging examination component of the study was not perfect (On-line Table 1) and showed attrition at the last visit point.
items.reasoning: While 136 datasets were analyzed, the drop from 28 to 19 subjects in some 6-month metrics represents a ~32% loss, which is significant.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not describe specific efforts made to retain or follow up with participants who missed visits.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The authors mention attrition but do not list specific reasons (e.g., moved away, withdrew consent) for individual dropouts.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no comparison provided between the characteristics of those who completed the 6-month visit and those who did not.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: A necessary mathematic assumption applied to the statistical analysis in this study is that the missing data are randomly distributed between the analysis groups.
items.reasoning: The authors assume no difference (Missing at Random), but do not provide empirical data to support this assumption.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (concussion/injury status) is well-defined, and the QSM measurement technique is described with high technical detail, including artifact mitigation and stability thresholds.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Athletes were imaged within 24 hours after injury, followed by examinations at 8 days and 6 months postinjury.
items.reasoning: The 'exposure' is the sports-related concussion, with clear timing for measurements.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: QSM data were collected by saving the raw k-space data from a commercially available SWI application... susceptibility inversion was performed using an adapted localized processing formulation of the morphology-enabled dipole inversion (MEDI) algorithm.
items.reasoning: The study uses sophisticated, standardized MR sequences and validated algorithms (MEDI) for measurement.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: White matter was defined as - 0.03 ppm, and subcortical iron-rich regions were defined as -0.05 ppm.
items.reasoning: The authors used pre-defined susceptibility thresholds based on literature/control means rather than post-hoc optimization.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Imaging was performed on a clinical 3T MR imaging scanner using a 32-channel head receive array.
items.reasoning: All subjects were imaged using the same hardware and protocol.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the 143 acquired QSM datasets, only 7 were removed due to motion-related quality control checks.
items.reasoning: A very high percentage of acquired scans were usable for analysis.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study does not appear to use imputation; it uses a linear mixed effects model which handles missing data but does not 'impute' values.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes include standardized clinical tools (SCAT-3, SAC) and Return-to-Play (RTP) duration, which are standard in concussion research. The measurement methods were consistent across groups.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The Sport Concussion Assessment Tool, 3rd ed (SCAT-3) symptom checklist, the Standardized Assessment of Concussion (SAC), and the Balance Error Scoring System were also collected at each visit.
items.reasoning: Standardized clinical outcomes and follow-up intervals (24h, 8d, 6m) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: SCAT-3, SAC, Balance Error Scoring System, and RTP measures on the full study cohort are also presented
items.reasoning: These are validated, standard-of-care instruments for concussion assessment.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: collected at each visit.
items.reasoning: The protocol for clinical assessment was applied uniformly to both cohorts at the specified time points.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study matches controls and accounts for prior concussions, the lack of baseline (pre-injury) imaging is a significant source of potential confounding, as individual baseline susceptibility is unknown.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Table 2: Age, Weight, Height, Y.I.S., G.P.A., P.SRC
items.reasoning: Key demographic and history variables were measured, but acute treatment/medication post-injury was not detailed.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: P.SRC, number of previous sports-related concussions; ... diagnosed prior concussion within 6 months
items.reasoning: Confounders like prior injury history are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: history of prior diagnosed sports-related concussions
items.reasoning: Relies on 'diagnosed' history, which may be subject to recall bias or under-reporting in athletes.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Subjects provided written consent... subset of 56 subjects... split evenly
items.reasoning: Baseline data collection was standardized for both groups.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No imputation for confounders is mentioned.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: split evenly across injured and matched control athletes
items.reasoning: The use of a matched control group from the same athletic environment helps control for many environmental confounders.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: Pearson correlations between the first time point susceptibility values and prior SRC history were computed... history of prior concussion is not a strong determinant
items.reasoning: They analyzed the impact of prior concussions, but the primary group comparisons (t-tests) were not adjusted for all baseline variables simultaneously.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is robust, utilizing linear mixed effects models to account for longitudinal data and random effects. Multiple comparison corrections (FDR) were applied to subregional analyses.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Longitudinal trends of the susceptibility means were assessed using a linear mixed effects model with random effects terms.
items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline from registration to ROI analysis to the final model is well-documented.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: mean ROI susceptibility was the response variable and the direct fixed predictor terms were group (injured versus control) and visit. An interaction fixed predictor term, group visit, was also included
items.reasoning: The model correctly targets the interaction between injury and time, which is the standard for longitudinal prognosis studies.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: linear mixed effects model with random effects terms... modeled for subject variation by group and subject variation by visit.
items.reasoning: Mixed models are the gold standard for handling longitudinal data with missing observations.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Table 4 summarizes the group susceptibility effects for several regions... P values for the subregional analyses are reported without multiple-comparison corrections [and with].
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant findings (e.g., gray matter) and provide both raw and FDR-corrected p-values.
